title: Are Plastic Water Heaters Worth It? This Old House – Plastic-Tank vs Glass-Lined Steel Comparison

locations.name: North Carolina
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly places Stacey in North Carolina

locations.name: home center (hardware store)
locations.basis: Transcript states she walked into the home center; used as a location reference

summary: This Old House hosts evaluate whether a plastic water heater is a worthwhile upgrade by contrasting a 50-gallon plastic-tank unit with a traditional glass-lined steel tank. The discussion covers upfront cost (~$1,200), the plastic tank’s lifetime warranty on the tank, and improved insulation, then contrasts corrosion protection (anode rods) and maintenance implications (heating element replacements) with the conventional tank. They quantify modest electrical efficiency gains (about 5–10%), note that the warranty on plastic tanks often applies only to the tank itself, and emphasize weighing the economics against anticipated, long-term occupancy in the home when making a purchase decision.
